channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Thoma Bravo's Rhode Tries to Keep Pace of Dealmaking High
item.description: A.J. Rohde, senior partner at Thoma Bravo, joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." They discuss how Thoma Bravo has kept up an intense pace of dealmaking with three deals in six weeks. Notably, Thoma Bravo agreed to take Accelerant private. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX Attempted to Buy AI Coding Startup Cognition
item.description: SpaceX approached Cognition AI Inc. about a potential acquisition to gain ground in the AI race, according to people familiar with the matter. Ed Ludlow has more on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Car-Seller Copart Is Among Suitors for Software Firm CCC
item.description: Bloomberg's Ryan Gould joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Copart is in talks to acquire CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc., the car-insurance software provider that has been weighing selling itself, according to people familiar with the matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Private Capital to Drive AI Infrastructure Financing
item.description: Sitara Sundar, Head of Alternative Investment Strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discussed the evolving landscape of AI infrastructure financing, highlighting the significant role of private markets alongside public markets. She explained that a substantial portion of the multi-trillion dollar investment needed over the next five years for AI infrastructure, such as data centers, compute power, and grid enhancements, will come from private capital, estimated at around 25%. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SpaceX Attempted to Acquire AI Coding Startup Cognition
item.description: SpaceX approached artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. about a potential acquisition, according to people familiar with the matter, in what would have been its second large takeover in recent months to gain ground in the AI race.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas, Ed Ludlow and Rebecca Torrence

item.title: AI Chip Startup Fractile in Talks for $6.5 Billion Value After Anthropic Deal
item.description: Fractile, a startup developing chips tailored for artificial intelligence use that has a deal to supply Anthropic PBC, is in advanced talks to notch a valuation more than six times higher than the price it landed in May.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence and Dina Bass

item.title: Marvell, Google Deepen Ties in AI Chip Race | Bloomberg Tech 8/19/2026
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at the expanded partnership between Marvell and Google for chip development, with Marvell giving the search giant the right to buy as much as $12.2 billion in stock. Plus, SK Hynix plans to buy back $29 billion of shares and return more profits to investors to stabilize its stock after falling more than 50% in two months. And, startup Fuse raises $100 million to bring commercial nuclear fusion energy to the US and its allies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investors Bet on Making Commercial Fusion a Reality
item.description: Fuse has raised $100 million to accelerate development and commercialization of its fusion technology. CEO JC Btaiche joins Bloomberg to discuss why the company is focused on building generators faster, and why he sees private companies as critical to helping the US compete with China in the race for fusion energy. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why AI Isn’t the BOE’s Biggest Inflation Worry
item.description: Could the AI boom become a new source of inflation for the UK? KPMG UK Chief Economist Yael Selfin discusses how rising chip and AI model costs are filtering through the economy and why higher household energy costs remain a much bigger concern for the Bank of England. She joins Ed Ludlow to discuss on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI to Enhance Safety Processes for Paid Tool Customers
item.description: OpenAI said it will enhance safety processes for paying users who have access to its most advanced artificial intelligence models, stepping up its safeguards at a time when customers are entrusting AI with more complex tasks and sensitive information.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Unitree Robotics Surges in Shanghai Debut
item.description: Unitree Robotics shares surged in their Shanghai trading debut after the company raised 6.1 billion yuan in an initial public offering, becoming the first listed humanoid robot maker in mainland China. Bloomberg's Peter Elstrom joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Pre-IPO Credit Facility to Rise Over $10 Billion
item.description: Anthropic's revolving credit facility is anticipated to rise above its approximately $10 billion target, according to sources. That's a substantial increase over a $2.5 billion five-year facility the AI company secured last year, though discussions are still ongoing. Bloomberg's Sridhar Natarajan joins Ed Ludlow with the details on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Shocks Markets With Bigger Buybacks | Open Interest 8/19/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent surprises markets with a major boost to debt buybacks as yields hit multi-year highs. SK Hynix surges on a nearly $30 billion buyback. Moderna and Merck jump on promising melanoma vaccine results. Plus, Target and Lowe’s report, with Walmart still ahead. Telsey's Joseph Feldman joins us on the retail winners and losers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Moderna and Merck Revive mRNA Hopes With Melanoma Success
item.description: A personalized vaccine developed by Moderna Inc. and Merck & Co. reduced the recurrence of melanoma in a large, late-stage trial, raising expectations for treating the deadliest form of skin cancer and showing the promise of the embattled mRNA technology. Bloomberg's Sam Fazeli joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Healthcare Stands Out Beyond AI
item.description: UBS's Nadia Lovell said that as AI influences more sectors across the market, traditional diversification has become more challenging, making healthcare an attractive option due to its strong performance, innovation pipeline, and relatively attractive valuations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ex-Meta Staffer Says Daughter, 14, Was Prey on Instagram
item.description: Arturo Béjar spent six years working on child safety tools at Meta Platforms Inc.’s Facebook, but told a jury he did not fully understand the threats posed to young users on the platform until his 14-year-old daughter signed up for an Instagram account.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg and Isaiah Poritz (Bloomberg Law)

item.title: T-Mobile Cyber Staff Chopped Cable After Finding Chinese Hack
item.description: Salt Typhoon revelations inspired an internal investigation.
item.dc:creator: Jake Bleiberg

item.title: Marvell Gives Client Google Right to Buy $12.2 Billion Stock
item.description: Marvell Technology Inc. has agreed to give Alphabet Inc.’s Google rights to buy as much as $12.2 billion of its shares in exchange for purchasing chips.
item.dc:creator: Dana Wollman

item.title: China Accuses EU of Overreach in JD.com Probe, Warns of Reprisal
item.description: China criticized the European Union for its use of the Foreign Subsidies Regulation to probe JD.com Inc.’s planned €2.2 billion takeover of German electronics retailer Ceconomy, calling it an “improper extraterritorial jurisdiction” and prohibiting compliance with the measures.
item.dc:creator: Foster Wong

item.title: SK Hynix Moves to Calm Market With $29 Billion Share Buyback
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. unveiled plans to buy back 40 trillion won ($29 billion) of shares and return more profits to investors, moving to stabilize its shares after they fell more than 50% in two months.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee and Denny Thomas
